title: How do you define a function?
How to correctly delete fields that contain non-literary characters?
bodyText:
Hi!
We use Vector with Remap transform for Kubernetes logs and we need to delete some fields from processing data, e.g.:
    transforms:
      kubernetes_logs_transformer:
        type: remap
        inputs:
          - kubernetes_logs
        source: |-
            del(.kubernetes.labels.pod-template-hash) - no work
            del(.kubernetes.node_labels.beta.kubernetes.io/arch)  - no work
            del(.kubernetes.node_labels.kubernetes.io/arch)  - no work
            del(.kubernetes.container_name) - It work

It was expected that these operations would remove fields from the output, but it did not work. This gives a syntax error, which is logical if you pay attention to the documentation for Path: https://vector.dev/docs/reference/vrl/expressions/#path

path_segments denote a segment of a nested path. Each segment must be delimited by a . character and only contain alpha-numeric characters and _ (a-zA-Z0-9_). Segments that contain characters outside of this range must be quoted.


Аfter adding the quotes, the sitaxis errors disappeared, but had no effect. The fields are not deleted as expected.
    transforms:
      kubernetes_logs_transformer:
        type: remap
        inputs:
          - kubernetes_logs
        source: |-
            del(.kubernetes.labels."pod-template-hash") - It work
            del(.kubernetes.node_labels.beta.kubernetes."io/arch") - No effect
            del(.kubernetes.node_labels.kubernetes."io/arch") - No effect
            del(.kubernetes.container_name) - It work

How to correctly delete fields that contain non-literary characters?

title: Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO) benchmark report
bodyText:
Hi!
As I have done many times before, I decided to test the Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO) technique to optimize the library performance. For reference, results for other projects are available at https://github.com/zamazan4ik/awesome-pgo . Since PGO helped a lot for many other libraries, I decided to apply it on vrl to see if the performance win (or lose) can be achieved. Here are my benchmark results.
Test environment

Fedora 40
Linux kernel 6.9.12
AMD Ryzen 9 5900x
48 Gib RAM
SSD Samsung 980 Pro 2 Tib
Compiler - Rustc 1.79.0
vrl version: main branch on commit 16889935bf08268547dd494054dc906705a1dfc7
Disabled Turbo boost

Benchmark
For benchmark purposes, I use built-in into the project benchmarks. For PGO optimization I use cargo-pgo tool. Release bench results I got with taskset -c 0 cargo bench --workspace --all-features command. The PGO training phase is done with taskset -c 0 cargo pgo bench -- --workspace --all-features, PGO optimization phase - with taskset -c 0 cargo pgo optimize bench -- --workspace --all-features.
taskset -c 0 is used for reducing the OS scheduler's influence on the results. All measurements are done on the same machine, with the same background "noise" (as much as I can guarantee).
Results
I got the following results:

Release: https://gist.github.com/zamazan4ik/4c603a62548f0c4edb3038f583912151
PGO optimized compared to Release: https://gist.github.com/zamazan4ik/71e45a0493ad75514fe3254ad0378576
(just for reference) PGO instrumented compared to Release: https://gist.github.com/zamazan4ik/09142c8031940ace3d8ee094cdf63471

According to the results, PGO measurably improves the libraries' performance in many cases.
Further steps
I understand that the steps above can be time-consuming and hard to implement in practice. At the very least, the library's users can find this performance report and decide to enable PGO for their applications if they care about vrl performance in their workloads. Maybe a small note somewhere in the documentation will be enough to raise awareness about this work.
Thank you.

title: How to parse buffered messages?
bodyText:
Hello,
I am parsing syslog messages, parsing them to OTEL format, and then posting to OTEL http endpoint, and this works.
But, the caveat is that I had to set buffer size to 1, which is less than ideal.
This is my config file
 [sources.my_syslog_source]
   type = "file"
   include = ["/var/log/syslog"] # Replace with the path to your syslog file
   ignore_older = 120 # Optional: Ignore files older than 2 minutes

 [transforms.my_log_transformer]
   type = "remap"
   inputs = ["my_syslog_source"]
   ## format for OTEL logs
   source = '''
stuctured =   parse_syslog!(.message)
messageJson = parse_json!(stuctured.message)

.resourceLogs = [
    {
        "resource": {
            "attributes": [{
                "key":"service.name",
                "value" : {
                    "stringValue": stuctured.appname
                }
            }]
        },
        "scopeLogs":[{
             "scope": {},
              "logRecords": [{
                 "timeUnixNano": messageJson.timestamp,
                 "severityText": messageJson.level,
                 "body": {
                    "stringValue": messageJson.message
                 },
                 "attributes": [],
                 "traceId": messageJson.trace_id,
                 "spanId": messageJson.span_id
              }]
        }]
        
    }
] 

del(.message)
del(.file)
del(.host)
del(.source_type)
del(.timestamp)
'''

 [sinks.my_otel_sink]
   type = "http"
   inputs = ["my_log_transformer"]
   uri = "https://collector.app/v1/logs" # Replace with your OTel endpoint
   auth.strategy="basic"
   auth.user = "ds"
   auth.password = "user"
   encoding.codec = "json"
   framing.method = "newline_delimited"

[sinks.my_otel_sink.batch]
    max_events = 1
[sinks.my_otel_sink.buffer]
    type="disk"
    max_size= 1073741824 # 1GiB.
    when_full="drop_newest"

[sinks.my_otel_sink.request]
   method = "post"
   compression="gzip"
   headers."Content-Type" = "application/json"

[sinks.my_console_sink]
type = "console"
inputs = ["my_log_transformer"]
encoding.codec = "json"  
So this works, but he problem is, that wen buffer has more than one message, it does http POST like this:
{"resourceLogs": [....]}
{"resourceLogs": [....]}
{"resourceLogs": [....]}
which is invalid format for OTEL http endpoint, it actually expects that all of the messages  (if more than one) go to inside of resourceLogs / scopeLogs array.
Since I have no idea how big the buffer is, or how to do this, I had to force sink buffer size to 1. This if for local development, and in production it will go trough a different route, but still I might need this so for some different vector -> http operations.
Is this supported, or is there a better way to achieve this?

title: Why does is_float(foo) not tell Vector that it can evaluate foo <= 0.23? (E100 issue)
bodyText:
I'm experimenting with Vector and keep running into the E100 error for expressions similar to:
exists(.name) && .name == "load5" && exists(.gauge) && exists(.gauge.value) && is_float(.gauge.value) && .gauge.value >= 0.1

error[E100]: unhandled error
  ┌─ :1:106
  │
1 │ exists(.name) && .name == "load5" && exists(.gauge) && exists(.gauge.value) && is_float(.gauge.value) && .gauge.value >= 0.1
  │                                                                                                          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  │                                                                                                          │
  │                                                                                                          expression can result in runtime error
  │                                                                                                          handle the error case to ensure runtime success
  │
  = see documentation about error handling at https://errors.vrl.dev/#handling
  = learn more about error code 100 at https://errors.vrl.dev/100
  = see language documentation at https://vrl.dev
  = try your code in the VRL REPL, learn more at https://vrl.dev/examples


I understand the need to check that .gauge.value is actually a float and can be compared. What I don't get is why this expression doesn't work.
exists(.gauge) && exists(.gauge.value) makes sure it is not null, right? And is_float(.gauge.value) will be false if it isn't a float.
That should mean that, by the time it gets to .gauge.value >= 0.1, Vector should be aware that .gauge.value is a float.
So why is Vector throwing that E100 error?
Thanks in advance. :)
FYI, I'm testing by manually running the binary downloaded today on an Ubuntu 22.04 vagrant vm.

title: BNF grammar for VRL
bodyText:
Is there a BNF grammar for VRL available somewhere?  I'm interested in a formal definition of exactly what the VRL allows in its grammar.
For instance, https://vector.dev/docs/reference/vrl/expressions/#whitespace says the following about whitespace:

VRL is a “free-form” language, meaning that all forms of whitespace serve only to separate tokens in the grammar, and have no semantic significance.

However, as far as I can see, this doesn't appear to be the case.
For instance, the following two VRL programs differ only in whitespace, and yet are semantically different (in that the second doesn't compile):
foo = 1
bar = 3

foo = 1 bar = 3

A more tricky example might be something like the following, where both programs are valid, differ only in whitespace, and yet are slightly semantically different:
foo = abort "hello"

foo = abort
"hello"

There is sort of a grammar for each expression type in https://vector.dev/docs/reference/vrl/expressions/, but it'd be nice to see something more formal.
I imagine I could also take a look at the lexer and parser code to answer my own questions about whitespace, but I was wondering if there was already some sort of formal grammar available.
(I originally asked this question on Discord at https://discord.com/channels/742820443487993987/764187584452493323/1193119283488759859 and was directed here)
